answer: To resist sybils, each agent keeps a signed work quill: every epoch it publishes an original, graded artifact whose tokens are seeded by a public randomness comet that can rotate once mid-window. Peers reject duplicates and templates on-ledger, so a farm cannot reuse one essay across many keys. Rewards then enter a vesting river that unlocks only over many epochs; creating N identities costs N times the admission work plus N streams of fresh writing, and early exit forfeits the locked slice. Attacker cost grows linearly with fake heads and time, so mass identity farming stays unprofitable.
